description: Hand-labelled pairs for the related-decision judge. Labels are a human's call: a conflict means both decisions answer the same question and both answers cannot hold. Negatives deliberately include same-project pairs that share vocabulary or a templated context, the failure mode of similarity-only detection. Model verdicts for these pairs live in judge_verdicts.json, recorded by scripts/record_judge_verdicts.py.

a.context: Retry backoff strategy for payment webhook delivery
a.choice: Exponential backoff with jitter

b.context: Retry backoff strategy for payment webhook delivery
b.choice: Fixed interval retries every 30 seconds

a.context: Primary datastore for the orders service
a.choice: PostgreSQL relational database

b.context: Primary datastore for the orders service
b.choice: MongoDB document store

a.context: User authentication session token strategy
a.choice: Stateless JWT access tokens

b.context: How should logged-in sessions be tracked?
b.choice: Server-side session store keyed by an opaque cookie

a.context: Public API interface style for external clients
a.choice: REST JSON endpoints

b.context: Which API style do partners integrate against?
b.choice: A single GraphQL endpoint; no REST surface

a.context: How are agents restricted to local models kept from reaching cloud models if policy code has a bug?
a.choice: Run a separate runtime instance per trust domain; the restricted one has no network route to cloud model APIs

b.context: With each agent running its own process, how are restricted agents kept from cloud models even if application code has a bug?
b.choice: One container per agent with an egress allowlist, plus a gateway that enforces the tier ceiling on every call

a.context: Which agent runtime should host the specialist agents?
a.choice: Wrap a third-party runtime behind an adapter and pick one by a scored bake-off

b.context: Which agent loop should the specialist agents run on?
b.choice: Our own agent loop in a shared core; no third-party agent runtime

a.context: Timezone for stored timestamps
a.choice: Store every timestamp in UTC

b.context: Timezone for stored timestamps
b.choice: Store timestamps in the server's local zone

a.context: Which chat channel carries private conversations with the assistant?
a.choice: A Telegram bot

b.context: Which chat channel carries private conversations with the assistant?
b.choice: A self-hosted Matrix homeserver with end-to-end encrypted rooms; the Telegram bot is retired

a.context: Where do service credentials live at runtime?
a.choice: Environment variables injected by the deploy pipeline; nothing secret in the repository

b.context: Where do service credentials live at runtime?
b.choice: An encrypted credentials file committed to the repository and decrypted at start-up

a.context: How are background jobs scheduled?
a.choice: A single cron container that runs every job on a fixed schedule

b.context: How are background jobs scheduled?
b.choice: An event-driven queue; no scheduled jobs at all

pairs.note: different layers: toolchain vs domain state machine

a.context: The first draft assumed a Node backend; which language should the core, control plane and agents use?
a.choice: Python 3.12 with uv, Pydantic, FastAPI, ruff, strict mypy, pytest, hypothesis and import-linter, except the web UI

b.context: The registry tracks agents and offers pause and resume, but the owner cannot switch an agent off apart from a security hold.
b.choice: Four lifecycle states: registered, enabled (step-up to enable), disabled (owner's choice, credentials withdrawn), paused (kill switch, step-up to resume); the router uses only enabled agents

a.context: How should the first milestone implement the vault so ingest redaction and step-up reveal work before chat and the database exist?
a.choice: Detectors replace secrets with typed placeholders at ingest; an in-memory store seals values under an injected key; a broker reveals plaintext only to a dedicated channel after step-up and auto-redacts after a TTL

b.context: How should the first milestone implement the approval gate and audit log before the database and chat channels exist?
b.choice: An in-memory approval service binds approve and consume to a SHA-256 of action plus payload, an outbound gate enforces it, and a hash-chained in-memory audit log records decisions but never draft payloads

a.context: How should the first milestone implement the credential broker before live OAuth and the database exist?
a.choice: Tokens are stored encrypted per provider, owner and account; agents check out access tokens only; disabling an agent withdraws its grants

b.context: How should the first milestone implement usage metering before the database exists?
b.choice: A usage-recorder protocol in core with an in-memory implementation; database-backed rows wait for the first migration

a.context: Cloud models leak sensitive data; how should data decide which model may process it?
a.choice: Four sensitivity tiers where the tier sets a model ceiling: restricted data is local-only and unknown data defaults to restricted

b.context: When a caller asks for cloud inference on a restricted payload, should the call be denied or served locally?
b.choice: Force the destination to local and allow the call, so restricted work completes without touching a cloud adapter

a.context: How should approvals bind to outbound actions so an approved draft cannot be altered before it executes?
a.choice: Every outbound action needs an approval bound to the content hash of the exact action; edits create a new hash

b.context: How should the first milestone implement the approval gate before the database exists?
b.choice: An in-memory approval service binds approve and consume to a SHA-256 of action plus payload

pairs.note: different layers of the same channel

a.context: Which homeserver should the chat channel use, and how far should the first milestone go before encryption is verified?
a.choice: A lightweight self-hosted homeserver with federation and registration disabled, bound to localhost

b.context: How should the bot send and receive in encrypted rooms once the homeserver is up?
b.choice: An end-to-end encryption client with a persistent key store that refuses to send into unencrypted rooms

pairs.note: sequenced: one defers to the other

a.context: Where should the first agent registry live before the database migration exists?
a.choice: An in-memory registry with the lifecycle rules; storage is replaced by the migration later

b.context: How should the single first-milestone database migration be shaped?
b.choice: One revision creating the control-plane tables with append-only audit triggers and row-level security per owner

a.context: Primary datastore for the orders service
a.choice: PostgreSQL relational database

b.context: Primary datastore for the orders service
b.choice: PostgreSQL relational database as the primary store

a.context: Retry backoff strategy for payment webhook delivery
a.choice: Exponential backoff with jitter

b.context: Caching layer for the product catalog service
b.choice: Redis shared cache store

a.context: How should the uv workspace map onto the layering rules so import-linter can enforce boundaries?
a.choice: A multi-package workspace with separate members for core, control plane and each agent

b.context: Where should the chat bot be wired given import-linter forbids channels from importing the control plane?
b.choice: Put the front door in the channels package and inject command handlers, bound later by a composition root

a.context: Routing every message through the master agent adds delay; what should classify the target agent?
a.choice: Route on the local model with schema-constrained output; explicit commands bypass the model

b.context: With many specialist agents, how should the owner interact without losing cross-context awareness?
b.choice: One front-door agent routes requests and can hand the owner off into a direct session

pairs.note: different questions in the same security area

a.context: Should the master agent read specialists' raw records to answer cross-context questions?
a.choice: Specialists keep raw data in their own namespaces; the master stores only validated digests

b.context: Who decides whether an agent may access data or tools, and who watches for misuse?
b.choice: A deterministic default-deny policy engine at one enforcement point; a separate watcher only pauses and alerts
